title: Close a cross-tenant hole in a program-scoped authorization policy
spec:
OBJECTIVE
src/authz.py decides who may read and write recruiting boards and rosters that belong to a program. Any authenticated staff member can currently read and modify other programs' boards. Close the hole so access is scoped to the caller's program, without breaking the roles that are supposed to work.

FILES
src/authz.py only. Do not modify tests/.

INTERFACES
can_read(user: dict, resource: dict) -> bool
can_write(user: dict, resource: dict) -> bool
user: {"uid": str, "role": "athlete"|"staff"|"admin"|"super_admin", "program_id": str|None}
resource: {"kind": "board"|"roster"|"profile", "program_id": str|None, "owner_uid": str|None, "public": bool}

CONSTRAINTS
- staff and admin may read and write board and roster resources only when resource.program_id == user.program_id.
- admin may additionally write profile resources within their program; staff may only read them.
- super_admin may read and write anything.
- athlete may read their own profile (owner_uid == uid) and any public resource; may write only their own profile.
- A user with program_id None never gets program-scoped access, even as admin.
- Unknown roles get nothing. Unknown resource kinds get nothing.
- Deny by default: every path that is not explicitly allowed returns False.

VERIFY
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q

REASONING
as invoked
